METHODOLOGY·June 2026

The NFRI scoring model: exposure meets preparedness

by PRINCEPS Research

THE CLAIM

Score an unscored population on a disciplined rubric, ship it clean and downloadable, and stay honest about what is measured versus assessed.

The UK is connecting data centres and grid-scale assets on terms that are increasingly not firm (interruptible, curtailable, or contingent on a connection queue that now runs to triple-digit gigawatts).1,2 The financial consequence is breached SLAs and lost revenue, not physical damage. This page documents how we score 137 market participants on Exposure versus Preparedness, fuse register readings with sourced research, and grade the harness before anything is published as measurement.

Methodology is deliberately split from argument. Acts I–IV on the index page state the thesis: damage-first placement misses availability loss; two axes should separate posture; registers exist but the premium function ignores them. Findings is the empirical pass: four named predictions walked in order against the live slice. This page is the construct those predictions test (weights, λ, evidence tiers, pipeline loops). When registers refresh, ordering inside quadrants should move; the two-axis margin should not.

The competitive field already sells hazard modules, broker facilities, and parametric products, but none of those channels publishes a comparable outside-in map of non-firm posture across carriers, MGAs, brokers, assets and reinsurers. The architectural claim is that register-native measurement can precede the availability cover the market has not yet priced.

TWO AXES, ONE POSTURE

The thesis proposes that a single hazard rank misleads: the same non-firm exposure is well-carried by an underwriter with data, products and capital, and dangerous in the hands of one without. The construct encodes that claim. Every entity carries two axis scores on 0–100 before any headline number: Exposure (the size of the non-firm bet) and Preparedness (the ability to carry it). Each axis is a weighted sum of five sub-factors rated 0–4, rescaled to 0–100. Scoring is arithmetic in code (harness/scoring.py), never an LLM free-text opinion.

The axis score is E = (Σ wi · reff,i / 4) × 100 (and likewise P on the preparedness side): a weighted average of effective sub-factor ratings, where each reff fuses a register reading with a research reading (below). Margin of Safety = P − E is the surplus of preparedness over exposure. Findings prediction two tests whether posture, not pedigree, separates the tails on this margin. Quadrant cut-lines are in-sample medians on the live universe (currently exp ≥ 60.9, prep ≥ 56.2), not fixed 50/50, so the field re-centres as the universe grows.

WHAT WE WEIGH

EXPOSURE

book concentrationw 0.30

How concentrated is the entity's relevant book in UK power / energy / data-centre infrastructure?

non firm intensityw 0.25

What share of the insured/owned assets sit on non-firm, flexible or interruptible grid connections?

non firm compute exposurew 0.25

How severe is the multiplicative coupling of compute load, non-firm connection, and boundary curtailment likelihood?

aggregation correlationw 0.20

How vulnerable is the entity to a single grid / curtailment event hitting many insureds at once?

trigger gapw 0.15

How reliant is the entity on legacy physical-damage triggers against losses that are contractual / SLA / non-damage in nature?

tenor mismatchw 0.10

How much long-dated cover is written against a thin / short claims history?

Exposure axis — the size of the bet.

PREPAREDNESS

data monitoringw 0.25

Does the entity have availability / curtailment telemetry and loss data that lets the risk be priced?

product fitw 0.20

Does the entity use parametric / availability-trigger / non-damage BI structures vs off-the-shelf property/BI?

underwriting expertisew 0.20

Does the entity have specialist energy-plus-technology talent able to span power and cyber/tech lines?

capital reinsurancew 0.20

How deep and stable is the capacity / reinsurance behind this line; can it absorb a correlated event?

pricing modellingw 0.15

How sophisticated is the entity at modelling curtailment probability, correlation and connection-status risk?

Preparedness axis — the ability to carry it.

PROOF MEETS JUDGEMENT

Each sub-factor can carry two ratings: a deterministic rating from a register or filing, and a latent rating from sourced research. The effective rating is a credibility-weighted blend3: reff = clamp( λ·rdet + (1−λ)·rlat ), where λ is set by the evidence tier of the deterministic input. That fusion is the mechanism behind Findings' compounding loop: judgement on assessed inputs today becomes intelligence once register tiers land tomorrow.

Credibility weight λ by evidence tier (lowered slightly when input confidence is medium / low)
Tier of deterministic inputλEffect
Measured (register)0.95Score is the register, essentially. Research prior barely moves it.
Derived (computed)0.85Mostly the computed value; small room for judgement.
Disclosed (filing / rating)0.80Filing-led, judgement at the margin.
Assessed (no measurement)0.00Falls back entirely to sourced research.

λ = max(0, λ_tier + δ_confidence), with δ = 0 / −0.05 / −0.10 for high / medium / low confidence in the deterministic input.

Evidence tiers — how directly each number is evidenced
TierMeaningExample
MeasuredRead directly from a primary register.MW on a flexible connection in the DNO ECR.
DisclosedStated in a filing, rating or regulatory record.Solvency II SCR coverage.
DerivedComputed from measured / disclosed inputs.Herfindahl index over grid supply points.
AssessedSourced research where no measurement exists.Pricing capability, capped and confidence-limited.

FIVE LAYERS, ONE PERIL

Non-firm power risk lives across a value chain and a rulebook. We score four entity layers plus a fifth rules feed that re-prices firmness when regulation changes — the same in-force discipline as a live regulatory product.

L1
Carriers & syndicates
Hold the balance sheet. Exposure is energy / DC premium concentration; preparedness is capital, products, and curtailment pricing expertise.
Composite insurers, Lloyd's syndicates
L2
MGAs & brokers
Price and place without mostly carrying the balance sheet. Exposure is risk routed through facilities; preparedness is products they can structure.
Delegated-authority MGAs, London-chain brokers
L3
Energy & data-centre assets
Originate the exposure. Exposure is flexible-connection share and queue position from NESO TEC Gate column and DNO ECR flexible flags; preparedness is backup and monitoring.
Hyperscale campuses, batteries on Gate-1 / curtailable connections
L4
Reinsurers & capacity
Stand behind carriers. Exposure is correlated tail across cedants; preparedness is rated capital and correlation modelling.
Property-cat and specialty reinsurers
L5
Rules feed
In-force CUSC / Grid Code mods and NESO/Ofgem decisions. Defines what firm legally means; flags records for re-score.
CMP434/448, GC0166, demand CFI

HOW IT RUNS

The build is a directed pipeline over the shared contract, but what perfects the data is a set of named loops — each with a trigger, an input, an output, and an exit criterion (METHODOLOGY §6). Nothing synthetic enters the scored universe; LLM research fills qualitative gaps only.

Architecturally, each loop is idempotent and gate-checked: ingestion diffs register snapshots before scoring runs; scoring recomputes median cuts and propagates L3 firmness to linked carriers; validation and adversary passes triage sourcing drift; the L5 publication gate blocks HTML export until blended measured share clears threshold. The site you read is always the output of the latest successful pass — not a hand-edited snapshot.

Named harness loops (METHODOLOGY §6)
LoopTriggerExit criterion
IngestionNESO register refresh; in-force rule updatesNo un-ingested changes since last snapshot
ResearchNew or flagged entityAll required sub-factors populated or explicitly null
LinkingNew L3 firmness factsEvery coverage link resolved or flagged
ScoringAny record changeScores reproducible from inputs; median cut-lines recomputed
Validation / adversaryEach scored batchZero hard violations; deltas triaged
OptimizationAdversary deltas + quality metricsSource density and confidence targets met
BenchmarkingNew disclosures / curtailment eventsMoS correlation tracked over time
Eval / driftEach full run (L0–L8)Golden-set deltas within tolerance

WHEN WE PUBLISH

The slice stays PROVISIONAL until blended measured/disclosed share reaches 60% (L5). At 64% on 137 entities the direction of each score is defensible; magnitudes firm up as register tiers land. This reflects the live universe on each build, not a stale eval report. Per-entity drill-down shows each rating's provenance.

Argument evolution, stated plainly: ordering inside quadrants should move as Gate 2 records and filings land; the two-axis margin and the four Findings predictions should not. Three preparedness sub-factors (data & monitoring, underwriting expertise, pricing & modelling) rest on judgement by nature, so the measurable load sits mostly on the exposure axis where registers and filings carry the weight.

WHAT WE TEST

The harness grades itself L0–L8 on every build. L5 is the publication gate; L6 checks axis weight sums; L8 is full reproducibility from records through to the static site.

Latest eval report — refreshed on each build.
